One shared cast · three selectable friends

“That’s the friend I play.”

All three appear together in the same videos. The child chooses whom to play during activities. No personalized video variants. Character concepts below are agreed; final reference artwork is still to be reviewed.

נבט

The curious friend

A small round moss creature with two broad leaf ears, an earthy green body and a cream face. Simple, readable silhouette.

First to investigate; pauses and listens when a friend needs help.

Signature gesture: Tilts both leaf ears toward a sound, then offers an open hand.

אדוה

The playful friend

A small rounded river creature with scalloped side fins, a slate-blue body and pale belly. Stays on the ground during gameplay.

Tries things enthusiastically; turns small surprises into shared laughter.

Signature gesture: Bounces once, splashes a toe, then looks back to invite the others.

זוהר

The thoughtful friend

A small rounded woodland creature with an amber belly patch and three simple light spots. Warm ochre, short limbs, no elaborate costume.

Notices what another creature is trying to communicate.

Signature gesture: Looks from a friend to an object, checks with a questioning chirp, then offers it.

Equal abilities; no character makes learning easier or harder. Final appearance must read clearly both in small gameplay portraits and in generated video.

Finale ↓

The video unlocks after completion, not a perfect score. Skipping does not block progress. An album lets children revisit unlocked videos. Educational prompts stay in activities; optional localized story captions accompany videos.

The final chapter · a gathering inside the great tree

Everyone has a place.

Stage 34 · MemoryUnderstand

Reconnect familiar words and meanings needed for the gathering.

Stage 35 · ShopHelp

Fulfill requests and gather the supplies. Video 8 shows the friends nearly ready.

Stage 36 · Magic HouseBring together

Place the final familiar objects. The canopy opens into a luminous garden; every friend’s voice joins the song.

The familiar Memory → Shop → House order becomes the final challenge. No extra boss game. No owl or flight ending. The view from the tree’s balcony reveals the communities we reconnected.

Start with what the game already has

Make the identity new. Reuse the learning.

The current art is already a useful foundation.

The live map has moonlight, warm windows and rounded storybook scenery. The playable cast includes a princess, dinosaur, puppy and unicorn. The new forest cast can use simple, readable shapes with richer atmospheric lighting in videos.

Shown here: an actual character asset, not the earlier profile-screen mockup.

Learning and progress requirements

Entrance. איפה נטייל היום? Two destinations with their own identities: עולם הפלאים and היער הלוחש. Use these destination names for implementation and keep them in editable UI copy. No repository name or version labels in the child-facing entrance.

Shared cast. Three new selectable forest friends appear as the same fixed group in every video. Selecting a friend changes gameplay representation, not the rendered movie. Current destination keeps its existing characters.

Language has a purpose. Understand a need → help through a learning activity → see the relationship and world change. The forest language is the selected English or Hebrew learning track; no invented vocabulary.

Wordless generated videos. AI-generated video shots, assembled into nine videos. Gestures, expressions, creature sounds, ambience and music. No dialogue, narration, subtitles, language-specific signs or lip-sync. Character movement is generated, not hand-animated.

Learning stays in gameplay. Preserve each learning track’s active runtime behavior. The current Hebrew activities use spoken prompts or target words with pictured choices. Videos remain wordless and never replace educational recordings or disclose a pending answer.

Tone and ending. Small friends, inviting scale, warm refuges and safe moonlit mystery. Language and cooperation bring the community together inside the tree. The opening canopy and illuminated landscape are the finale. No owl, giant bird guardian or flight ending.

Pacing. Opening; after newly completed stages 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30 and 35; ending after 36. These milestones cross curriculum chapter boundaries. Replays do not advance the story. Videos are skippable and replayable.

Production boundary. This deliverable is the storybook. No image/video generation, runtime changes, save migration or new entry screen implementation is included in this pass. Art and video production follow storybook review.

Independent journeys. Retain the current profile and character; store the forest choice and journey progress separately per profile and language. This is future implementation work.

Supported content. Example words in these scripts exist in the vocabulary catalog. Their exact stage pools still need authoring. Current House requests include book → shelf, book → table and apple → table; preserve the supported targets when dressing the room for the gathering.

Spend only after the story and pilot work

One small proof before a full production.

9

shared videos
for both learning tracks and all three friends

21

planned generated shots
about 126 seconds of finished story

0

new images or videos generated
during this storybook pass

  1. Story and cast concepts agreed. Review the reusable character reference artwork before commissioning scenes.
  2. Set the pilot limit before generating. Select the provider/model, verify its reference workflow, and agree a bounded cost and attempt limit.
  3. Generate one six-second pilot within that limit. Video 2, first shot: a resident recognizes an offered basket; a friend reacts. Test identity, gesture and a simple object handoff.
  4. Judge it without words. Is the meaning clear? Does the character match gameplay? Is the motion inviting and stable? Are there unwanted spoken words?
  5. Record actual cost and retries. Then decide whether to keep that model and agree the shot scope and spending ceiling for the remaining work. No unverified dollar estimate.
  6. Produce and assemble the videos. Character movement comes from video generation. Editing, music, creature sounds and sound-level adjustment complete one shared audiovisual master per milestone.

Cost depends on all billed attempts, including rejected shots, plus approved reference art and audio/editing work. Short shots and a fixed cast reduce scope; they do not guarantee consistency. The opening has a generated draft. Video 2’s garden-only plan is superseded by the village-and-courier revision.

How this differs from the first storyboard

Language understanding now causes each world change. The cast is shared with character selection. Scripts contain no dialogue or narration. The final four videos follow three tables and three blossoms: discover the hall, welcome the guests, finish preparing, then open the canopy. All owl and flight images are kept as reference material. The existing final three activities carry the finale. All previous generated images remain intact, including the owl. The final scripts define the story to implement.
